title: "Custom AMI"

# Why a custom AMI

ParallelCluster can install software when a node boots, but every minute spent installing is a minute a user waits for a session. Bringing up an EC2 instance and letting ParallelCluster configure it takes about 4 to 5 minutes. With all software baked into the AMI it stays at that; in an earlier setup that installed everything at boot time, it took more than 10 minutes.

The same AMI is used for the head node, the login nodes and the compute nodes.

# What is in the image

The image is built with ParallelCluster's [image builder](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/parallelcluster/latest/ug/building-custom-ami-v3.html) (EC2 Image Builder) on top of the official ParallelCluster **Ubuntu 24.04** image that matches your installed `pcluster` version.

`image/image-config.yaml` defines a single script component, `install-image.sh`. That script downloads the individual `install-*.sh` scripts from S3 and runs them through its `setup_something()` function:

| Script | Installs |
|---|---|
| `install-dummy.sh` | local `rstudio` user and the `rstudio-admins` / `rstudio-superuser-admins` groups, `sssd`/`realmd`/Kerberos, `adcli`, `pam_mkhomedir` |
| `install-r.sh` + `run.R` | multiple R versions from Posit's binaries, configured as below |
| `install-python.sh` | multiple Python versions (via `uv`), Jupyter, Posit Connect publishing |
| `install-quarto.sh` | Quarto |
| `install-os-deps.sh` | system libraries needed by common R packages, `squashfs-tools`, Google Chrome |
| `install-apptainer.sh` | Apptainer (for container sessions) |
| `install-nvidia.sh` | NVIDIA driver from the CUDA repository, only if the base image has none |

**All versions are pinned at the top of `image/install-image.sh`.** Edit them there before you build.

## R and Python

R and Python are installed from Posit's binaries ([R](https://docs.posit.co/resources/install-r.html), [Python](https://docs.posit.co/resources/install-python.html)), several versions side by side. The default version of each is symlinked into `/usr/local/bin`.

Each R version (configured by `image/run.R`):

-   uses the public [Posit Package Manager](https://packagemanager.posit.co) for CRAN and Bioconductor
-   uses a CRAN snapshot at most 60 days newer than the R release date
-   has the packages needed for the RStudio IDE integration preinstalled in a site library
-   uses a global `renv` cache in `/home/renv`, with the `renv`/`pak` integration enabled

Each Python version:

-   has Jupyter / JupyterLab and the Workbench integration installed
-   can publish to Posit Connect (`rsconnect_python`, `rsconnect_jupyter`)
-   uses PyPI via the public Posit Package Manager (`/etc/pip.conf`)

Install logs are written to `/opt/r-install.log` and `/opt/python-install.log` in the image.

## The `rc.pwb` cron job {#sec-rc-pwb}

`install-image.sh` also installs a root cron job that runs `/opt/rstudio/scripts/rc.pwb` every minute. The script itself is written to the shared `/opt/rstudio` EFS by the head node during cluster creation. On a login node, it runs `config-login.sh` once to install and start Workbench, and restarts Workbench whenever its `workbench-<hostname>.state` file is removed. It does nothing on other nodes.

This workaround is needed because ParallelCluster login nodes did not support `OnNodeConfigured` custom actions (see [aws-parallelcluster#5723](https://github.com/aws/aws-parallelcluster/issues/5723)).

# How to build the AMI

Prerequisites:

-   The Pulumi stack is deployed ([Pulumi](Pulumi.qmd)). The image build uses its S3 bucket, private subnet and SSH security group.
-   The ParallelCluster CLI is installed: run `uv sync` in the repository root and `source .venv/bin/activate`.

Then:

1.  Review the versions at the top of `image/install-image.sh`.
2.  Run

    ``` bash
    cd image
    ./build-image.sh <IMAGENAME> <PULUMI_STACK>
    ```

    where `<IMAGENAME>` is a name for the new image (letters, numbers and hyphens).
3.  Wait until the build has finished, then copy the AMI ID into the `AMI=` line of your `parallelcluster/envs/<name>.env`:

    ``` bash
    pcluster describe-image -i <IMAGENAME> | jq -r '.imageBuildStatus, .ec2AmiInfo.amiId'
    ```

# Debugging and housekeeping

## Build logs

``` bash
pcluster describe-image -i <IMAGENAME>
pcluster list-image-log-streams -i <IMAGENAME>
pcluster get-image-log-events -i <IMAGENAME> --log-stream-name <PCLUSTER_VERSION>/1
```

where `<PCLUSTER_VERSION>` is the version reported by `pcluster version`.

## Delete old images

``` bash
pcluster list-images --image-status AVAILABLE | jq -r '.images[].imageId'
pcluster delete-image -i <IMAGENAME>
```
